questions.question: As shown in the figure, a plane mirror is fixed at height of 50 cm from the bottom of tank containing water . The height of water in the tank is 8 cm. A small bulb is placed at the bottom of the water tank. The distance of image of the bulb formed by mirror from the bottom of the tank is :-
questions.explanation:
The bulb is placed at the bottom of a tank containing water of depth 8 cm, while a plane mirror is fixed 50 cm above the bottom. Due to refraction at the water-air interface, the bulb appears raised. The apparent depth of the bulb from the water surface  = 6 cm
Thus, the apparent position of the bulb is 8 – 6 = 2 cm above the bottom. The distance between this apparent object and the mirror is 50 – 2 = 48 cm
A plane mirror forms an image at the same distance behind it as object is in front.
Therefore, the image is formed 48 cm behind the mirror, 50 + 48 = 98 cm above the bottom of the tank.

The bond dissociation energy at the C–H bond for the compound :-
(I) CH3H                        (II) CH3–CH2–H
(III) CH2=CH–CH2–H  (IV) C6H5–H
questions.explanation:
Solution : C–H BDE decreases with increasing radical resonance stabilization and +H (hyperconjugation); sp3 C–H without stabilization is strong, allylic/benzylic stabilized are weak.
Compound analysis:
(I) CH3H : Highest BDE due to sp3 C–H with no resonance or +H stabilization of the radical.
(II) CH3 – CH2 – H: Slightly lower BDE than I; sp3 C – H with modest +H from adjacent alkyl.
(III) CH2 = CH – CH2 – H (allylic) : Lower BDE due to radical resonance stabilization (allylic).
(IV) C6H5 – H (benzylic) : Lowest BDE due to strong radical resonance stabilization with the aromatic ring.
The decreasing order of BDE is : I > II > III > IV.
Final answer : 1

Solution: Basicity depends on the availability of the lone pair on nitrogen. In options 2, 3, and 4, the nitrogen is directly attached to the benzene ring, causing the lone pair to delocalize into the ring through resonance, which significantly decreases basicity. In option 1 (Benzylamine), the nitrogen is attached to an aliphatic CH2 group; thus, the lone pair is localized and not involved in resonance. Localized lone pairs are much more available for donation to an acid.
